def: The 'brain' behind tools like ChatGPT, Claude and Copilot. It has read a huge amount of text and predicts good next words. It's brilliant with language, but it doesn't actually know today's prices or check facts unless it's given a tool to look them up.
An AI you have a conversation with. You ask, it answers. It doesn't go off and do things on its own.
A fixed recipe: 'when X happens, do Y'. Like a standing order at the bank. Reliable, but it can't cope with anything it wasn't set up for.
An AI you give a goal to, rather than a question. It works out the steps, uses tools (like your inbox or the web), checks its own work and hands the result back to you.
Whatever you type to an AI: a question, a request or a set of instructions.
The standing briefing you give an agent once, so you don't repeat yourself: who it works for, what its job is, how to sound and what it must never do.
Anything an agent can use to take a step: searching the web, reading your email, adding a row to a spreadsheet, creating a draft.
A link you approve between an AI tool and another account, such as Gmail or Google Drive. It's usually a 'Sign in with Google' style button. You can disconnect it at any time.
The behind-the-scenes way one piece of software talks to another. You don't need to touch one: connectors handle it for you.
The thing that sets an agent off: you pressing go, a time of day (a schedule) or something arriving (like a new enquiry email).
An agent job set to run at a regular time, such as 'every Monday at 7am'. It's like an alarm clock that starts the work.
Reference documents you give an agent, such as your price guide, FAQs, supplier notes or onboarding pack, so it answers from your material rather than guessing.
What an agent remembers between conversations, such as your preferences or past decisions. It's handy, but check what it has stored now and then.
A folder-like space in Claude or ChatGPT where you keep instructions and files for one job, so every chat inside it starts already briefed.
ChatGPT's name for a reusable assistant you set up with your own instructions and files.
When an AI states something confidently that is simply wrong or made up: a hotel that doesn't exist, a price it invented or a visa rule that's out of date. It's the main reason you stay in the loop.
A step where the agent stops and waits for you to check, edit or approve before anything goes out.
A rule that keeps an agent safe, such as 'never send, only draft' or 'never quote a price without saying it must be checked'.
A message the agent prepares but doesn't send. It sits in your drafts folder until you've read it and pressed send.
How some platforms meter usage. Each step an agent takes uses some up. When you run out, the agent pauses or you pay more.
A chain of steps across apps, such as 'new form, then spreadsheet row, then email'. Zapier calls them Zaps; Make calls them scenarios.
How hard it would be to move to a different platform later. Plain-text instructions move easily; complicated workflows have to be rebuilt.
The UK law on handling people's personal information. In short: only collect what you need, keep it safe, use it for the reason you gave and don't share it carelessly.
The UK rules on marketing by email, text and similar. Broadly, you need someone's consent before sending them marketing messages, and you must make opting out easy.
The UK advertising rules. Ads, including social posts promoting a business, must not be misleading, and earnings claims must be honest and typical.
The UK trade body for direct selling and network marketing. Its code expects honest recruitment, with no exaggerated income promises.
The UK government's official travel advice for every country (on GOV.UK), covering entry requirements, safety and health. It's always the source to check, not an AI.
The UK financial protection scheme for package holidays that include flights. If you sell these, there are rules about how you do it, usually handled through your host agency.
The UK travel trade association. Members follow a code of conduct on things like clear information and handling complaints.
A larger travel company that independent agents work under, often providing bookings systems, supplier deals and protection like ATOL. They may have their own rules on marketing and tools.
Sales tax. Many AI subscriptions show a price before VAT, and 20% is added at checkout in the UK.
